In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is equal to the source voltage. Therefore, the total voltage across the parallel resistors is 12 V.
The total resistance ($R_{total}$) is calculated using the reciprocal formula:
$$ \frac{1}{R_{total}} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2} + \frac{1}{R_3} $$
Substituting the given values:
$$ \frac{1}{R_{total}} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} $$
To add these fractions, find a common denominator (which is 12):
$$ \frac{1}{R_{total}} = \frac{3}{12} + \frac{2}{12} + \frac{1}{12} $$
$$ \frac{1}{R_{total}} = \frac{6}{12} $$
Simplifying the fraction:
$$ \frac{1}{R_{total}} = \frac{1}{2} $$
Taking the reciprocal to solve for $R_{total}$:
$$ R_{total} = 2 \text{ ohms} $$

From my own knowledge:
A double-acting cylinder has two ports (4 and 2) for extending and retracting. To extend, air enters port 4 and exits port 2. To retract, air enters port 2 and exits port 4.
The "Self-Return" feature is achieved by a 5/2 valve (V1). When the button is pressed, V1 opens to extend the cylinder. When the button is released, V1 closes, allowing air to escape from port 2. This drop in pressure causes the spring inside the cylinder to push the piston back to the start position.
The flow control (F2) ensures the cylinder extends at a controlled speed.

q: Write a Structured Text PLC program for a tank: open the fill valve when the low float switch comes on, and close it when the high float switch comes on.
why: the valve is not held open between the two floats
reply:
<title>ST: Tank Fill Valve Control</title>
language st

(* A tank fill valve control program using a simple state machine. *)
PROGRAM TankValveControl
VAR
    LowFloat AT %IX0.0 : BOOL;    (* TRUE: low water level *)
    HighFloat AT %IX0.1 : BOOL;   (* TRUE: high water level *)
    FillValve AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;   (* TRUE: valve open *)
    DrainPump AT %QX0.1 : BOOL;   (* TRUE: drain valve open *)
    FillAlarm AT %QX0.2 : BOOL;   (* TRUE: fill complete *)
END_VAR

VAR
    Phase : INT := 0;              (* 0: idle, 10: filling, 99: alarm *)
    InPhase : TON;
    LastPhase : INT := -1;
END_VAR

(* Initialize the phase timer to 2 minutes *)
InPhase(IN := (Phase = LastPhase), PT := T#2m);
LastPhase := Phase;

(* Main Control Logic *)
CASE Phase OF
    0:  (* Idle Phase *)
        IF LowFloat THEN Phase := 10;
        ELSIF HighFloat THEN Phase := 99;
        END_IF;
    10: (* Filling Phase *)
        IF HighFloat THEN Phase := 99;
        ELSIF InPhase.Q THEN Phase := 99;
        END_IF;
    99: (* Alarm Phase *)
        Phase := 99;
END_CASE;

(* Set outputs based on current phase *)
FillValve := (Phase = 10);
DrainPump := (Phase = 99);
FillAlarm := (Phase = 99);
END_PROGRAM
>>>
